raw_response:
I've been working this land for 30 years. I know Quzhou's soil — heavy on sand in spots, dry climate, groundwater that costs me electric money to pump. My children and daughter-in-law do factory work nearby, so the farm pressure is not crushing, but I still need to make it count. 10.9 mu is not a big operation. I have to be careful with inputs and water.

My plan: keep 7 mu in the wheat-maize rotation — that is my stable income, guaranteed market. Put the other 3.9 mu in cotton. Cotton is more work and more risk, but the price has been acceptable and I still have the labor knowledge from decades of doing it.

**Wheat**: I will use the improved variety we have been planting here for years — Jimai-series. No point switching. Four irrigations: before winter freeze, at jointing, heading, and grain fill. I will rotary-till in September before planting. Base fertilizer goes in at planting, urea topdress at jointing. Three pesticide sprays: one herbicide in late winter, one fungicide spray around jointing, one aphid spray at heading.

**Maize**: Plant directly into wheat stubble — no-till saves me time and fuel right at the busiest handover period. Hybrid seed, Zhengdan 958 or whatever seed shop has in stock locally. Summer rain helps but I will irrigate twice if needed — at seedling stage if it is dry and again at silking. Less fertilizer pressure than wheat on my fields.

**Cotton**: 3.9 mu. Spring rotation. Rotary till in April. Hybrid seed. Cotton eats more potassium on my soil type. Five pesticide applications — bollworm is still a problem here even with Bt cotton, and I watch for spider mites in August. Four irrigations: establishment, bud, flowering, boll development.
